notes: |sqrtT> = (|0> + e^{i pi/8}|1>)/sqrt 2 = Z(pi/8)|+>, the magic state of the square root of the T gate, at the fourth level of the Clifford hierarchy. It is not Clifford-equivalent to the H-type (edge) or T-type (face) orbits: its Bloch vector (cos(pi/8), sin(pi/8), 0) is neither an edge nor a face center of the stabilizer octahedron, and the Clifford group acts on Bloch vectors by signed coordinate permutations. Two basis states span it, and with the exact Galois lower bound of cert_sqrtt_galois.py this settles chi(|sqrtT>) = 2. Baseline under the board's rule: 1/2, published, from Theorem 2 of Qassim, Pashayan, and Gosset (arXiv:2106.07740), chi(R_theta^m) = O(2^{m/2}) for every angle theta (explicitly chi(R_theta^(24t+6)) <= 2^(12t+4)). The question the orbit asks is whether a finer phase is dearer per copy than the T state's log_2(3)/4 = 0.3963; the cells that would beat 1/2 are chi(|sqrtT>^5) <= 5 (0.4644) and chi(|sqrtT>^6) <= 7 (0.4680).
